aboutH2: Homewood Ravensview: Inpatient Addiction and Mental Health Care near Victoria, BC
intro: Homewood Ravensview is a private inpatient centre in North Saanich, on Vancouver Island's Saanich Peninsula, run by Homewood Health. It treats addiction alongside depression, anxiety, trauma, chronic pain and gambling disorder, and much of its work is with people who have several of these at the same time.

Addiction stays are six weeks and mental health or concurrent disorder stays are nine. Detox happens on site when it is needed, nurses are on shift around the clock, and you can call the intake team yourself without a doctor's referral.

pillars.title: A Mountainside Above the Saanich Peninsula
pillars.body: Ravensview sits on 28 acres of forest on a hill the W̱SÁNEĆ people call ȽÁU,WELṈEW, which the centre translates as place of refuge. The trails run straight into John Dean Provincial Park, and from the lounges and many of the rooms you look across farmland and water toward the mountains. Inside there is a gym, a yoga nook, art and music rooms and a library corner. Outside are tennis and pickleball courts, a horticulture garden, a meditation labyrinth and an outdoor cultural space. Homewood says it built the centre in partnership with local First Nation communities.

pillars.title: Aftercare Planning Starts at Admission
pillars.body: Discharge planning begins on the day you arrive. Everyone leaves with a written aftercare plan from a clinician, a place in a recovery management support group and membership in the Homewood Alumni Program, which is a virtual hub for ongoing learning. If you want more, the centre offers one-to-one counselling, step-down programming and substance use monitoring for an extra fee. For people going back to a job, the team can provide paperwork for employers or insurers and help plan a gradual return to work.

pillars.title: A Medical Team on Site Around the Clock
pillars.body: Care at Ravensview is led by physicians. The published team includes a medical director, psychiatrists, an addiction psychiatrist and an addiction physician, with nurses on site 24 hours a day. Therapy is done by master's level therapists, social workers and counsellors, plus art, music, horticultural and recreation therapists and occupational therapists. A registered dietitian runs the optional Therapeutic Teaching Kitchen, and a cultural liaison works with Nations across the country. Progress is tracked during the stay with Homewood Touchpoint, an online measurement tool.

overview: Ravensview is Homewood Health's inpatient centre in British Columbia; its other two centres are in Guelph, Ontario. It takes clients from across Canada, and the location suits people coming from Victoria, the rest of Vancouver Island and the Lower Mainland, since the airport and the Swartz Bay ferry are each about ten minutes away. Treatment draws on CBT, DBT, cognitive processing therapy and the Unified Protocol, with medication and detox when needed.

location.heading: Homewood Ravensview in North Saanich, British Columbia
location.intro: Homewood Ravensview is on McTavish Road in North Saanich, at the top of the Saanich Peninsula on Vancouver Island, with Sidney a few minutes away and downtown Victoria about 25 minutes south. From Vancouver it takes about 3 hours with the BC Ferries crossing from Tsawwassen to Swartz Bay, or you can fly into Victoria International Airport, 5 minutes from the centre; Nanaimo is about an hour and a half by road.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Homewood Ravensview cost?
faqs.a: Ravensview does not publish its fees. The centre says cost depends on how long you stay and which room you choose (semi-private, private or a private suite), and its intake team goes through the options with you on the first call. Recovery.com also lists no prices for it.

faqs.q: How long is the program at Homewood Ravensview?
faqs.a: Addiction treatment is a six-week inpatient stay. Treatment for depression, anxiety, trauma or concurrent disorders runs nine weeks. Every client also gets outpatient aftercare once they leave, according to the centre.

Yes. The centre says onsite withdrawal management and detox are available when a client needs them, so you do not have to arrange detox somewhere else first. A full assessment and treatment plan follow once detox is done.

faqs.q: Where is Homewood Ravensview and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Ravensview is at 1515 McTavish Road in North Saanich, on the Saanich Peninsula north of Victoria on Vancouver Island. It is about 5 minutes from Victoria International Airport, 10 minutes from the Swartz Bay ferry terminal and 25 minutes from downtown Victoria. Staff can pick you up at the airport or the ferry if you ask ahead.

faqs.q: Do I need a referral to go to Ravensview?
faqs.a: No. You can call the intake team yourself for a confidential conversation. The centre also takes referrals from physicians, therapists, psychologists, employers and employee assistance programs, and the intake team decides with you whether inpatient care is the right fit.

faqs.q: Is Ravensview covered by MSP or my benefits?
faqs.a: Ravensview is privately owned, so most people pay themselves or through employer coverage. The centre says some clients are funded through a provincial Ministry of Health, Workers Compensation Board or other third parties, and it accepts health identification cards from Veterans Affairs Canada and the RCMP. It is part of the WorkSafeBC Provider Network.

There are three. Cornerstone is the adult program. My Path is for young adults 19 and older, in small groups of people at the same stage of life. Guardians is for first responders, military members and veterans. Ravensview also runs a dedicated inpatient program for gambling disorder, including when no substance use is involved.

Every guestroom has an ensuite bathroom. Semi-private rooms are shared by two clients with a privacy divider, private rooms have a queen bed and a desk, and private suites have a king bed, extra living space and a glassed-in balcony. Meals are planned by a dietitian and a chef and served in a dining room that looks out over the forest.

faqs.q: What happens after I leave Ravensview?
faqs.a: Every client leaves with a structured aftercare plan written by a clinician, access to a recovery management support group and membership in the virtual Homewood Alumni Program. One-to-one counselling, step-down programming and substance use monitoring are also available afterwards at extra cost.

faqs.q: Can I use my phone or have visitors?
faqs.a: Not during the first week. Personal technology is held for the first 7 days and then allowed at set times. Visits start on the first Sunday after your first 7 days and run on Sundays from 2:30 to 4:30 p.m. in the lounges, dining room or on the grounds.

faqs.q: Is Ravensview the same as Homewood Health Centre in Guelph?
faqs.a: No. Both are run by Homewood Health, but Ravensview is a separate inpatient centre in North Saanich, BC, opened in 2019. Homewood Health Centre and The Residence at Homewood are in Guelph, Ontario, and have their own listings.
